paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 17a — Of Elazar ben Durdaya: "He said: The matter depends only on me. He placed his head between his knees and wept aloud until his soul departed. paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 5:5 — "He does not know with a knowledge that is outside Him, like people, who and their knowledge are two; rather He, may His Name be exalted, and His knowledge are one, and a person's mind cannot grasp this clearly. And just as a person cannot grasp and find the truth of the Creator, as it says, 'For man shall not see Me and live' (Shemos 33:20), so a person cannot grasp and find the Creator's knowledge. This is what the prophet said: 'For My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor your ways My ways' (Yeshayahu 55:8)."

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, end of the Tikkunim (Vayera) — Rabbi Yose asked: if a person is decreed righteous or wicked before he comes into the world, how can there be reward and punishment? "Rabbi Shimon said: This question is deep; the early ones disagreed over it, and many stumbled in it because they did not reach the depth of the secret… The secret of it is: all is foreseen, yet permission is granted." He explains: "All is foreseen in thought — the Holy One knows a person's thought — and permission is given to man in deed." He did not decree whether a person will be righteous or wicked; "the secret of the matter is deep: 'the hidden things belong to Hashem our God' (Devarim 29:28)." Rav Tzadok cites this passage for the principle that where there is knowledge there is no choice, and where there is choice there is no grasp of His knowledge (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 40; Takanas HaShavin 6:5; Resisei Layla 50:2).

p: where they asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:
From where do we know the revival of the dead
and that He knows what will be in the future?
both of them from this pasuk,
"Behold, you will lie with your fathers and rise;
"and this people will rise up and go astray"?
at least take half of it in your hands —
that He knows what will be in the future.
in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai,
that one derives both from it.
how can we learn both of them
Also, why was it necessary for Moshe Rabbeinu
that he will rise at the revival of the dead?
But the Gemara found it difficult
why there is any mention at all
of the statement "Behold, you will lie with your fathers."
had happened right after Moshe Rabbeinu's passing;
then it would fit to say
and afterward "and the people will rise up and go astray."
all the days of Yehoshua and the elders
for rising and standing for the good,
according to the explanation given here:
did not attain the fiftieth gate,
which belongs to the baal teshuvah,
And when it arose in the will of Hashem Yisbarach
also something of the fiftieth gate,
while the portion of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and to make him understand it,
"For I know that after my death
you will surely act corruptly," etc.
although Moshe Rabbeinu in truth knew
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu will in the future
for it is the fiftieth gate.
with which He will in the future revive the dead,
which is the Dew of Atika,
and this is what it says,
"Behold, you will lie with your fathers and rise."
He could reveal to him the Divine knowledge
that is in the fiftieth gate,
"and this people will rise up and go astray,"
that have been arranged and come
since the six days of Creation,"
And although once something is already written in the Torah
there is no longer free choice in it,
according to what the Rambam wrote
So too "and the people will rise up," etc.,
for every generation and for every individual.
And this is what is said
רְאוּ עַתָּה כִּי אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא
"See now that I, I am He,"
"I put to death and I bring to life;
I have wounded and I will heal"
it is stated in the holy Zohar
that there is One who is called the Cause of causes,
who is called the Cause above all causes,
and this is the aspect of the revelation of Atika,
"I put to death and I bring to life,"
from which it is expounded in the Gemara
from here is the revival of the dead.
"I have wounded and I will heal" —
"He will heal the wound of its blow"
the wound of the blow of the world
and the corruption of the serpent,
which is the blow of the world;
for one depends on the other;
and this will be in the future.
which is a semblance of the World to Come
and it can be that there are made
that in his own personal soul
